title: The mutation figures recorded for the notification-outbox substrate, cycles 1 and 2
note: Written at cycle 2 after the auditor found that cycle 1's dedup-key mutation did not reproduce and could not fail for the reason claimed. Every `find` is hand-written from the committed blob and occurs exactly once; replay refuses otherwise. `claimed_count` is the figure measured by the first replay on this tree and then re-checked by every replay since - a replay that disagrees is a finding, not a number to adjust. The `expected_failing_tests` names were transcribed from that first replay, after M2's original framing proved to test nothing: a key derived from the serialised payload cannot move when the order is amended, because the payload holds only a label and a primary key. M2 is therefore framed around what it can actually break - the event type, the occurrence discriminator, and canonical key ordering.

mutations.description: enqueue writes its row on transaction.on_commit instead of inside the caller's transaction, reopening the dual-write window this substrate exists to remove

_dedup_key returns a plain json.dumps of the payload: it drops the event type and the occurrence discriminator, and is no longer canonically ordered, so two call sites that build the same context differently produce different keys and a second reminder collapses into the first
_describe renders a set with str() instead of describing and sorting it, so the dedup key varies with PYTHONHASHSEED and the duplicate suppression does not hold across gunicorn workers
_load_reference catches only LookupError from apps.get_model, so a stored label it cannot parse (a.b.c raises ValueError there) escapes the documented error class and kills a drain loop mid-batch
_describe truncates an over-long value instead of refusing, which is what put a cut token or URL into a queued payload where it rendered as a working-looking link and failed at the customer
